Looking at this question about the paper "Cell size homeostasis is tightly controlled throughout the cell cycle" (PLOS Biology, 2023), I need to consider what assumption is made when comparing different forms of growth modulation on cell mass variation.

When studying how different growth modulation strategies (e.g., size-dependent vs. size-independent growth) affect cell mass, a critical assumption is needed to isolate the effect of the growth strategy itself. The researchers would need to assume that the cell cycle length is the same across the different growth modulation scenarios being compared, so that any observed differences in cell mass variation can be attributed to the growth modulation strategy rather than differences in timing.

This means the assumption is that cells divide at the same cell cycle length, allowing the researchers to specifically examine the impact of the growth modulation form on mass variation without confounding effects from different cycle durations.

[ANSWER]B[/ANSWER]
